title: Bases, positive cones and chambers of a real reflection set
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], $B:V\times V\to\mathbf R$ a bilinear form, and $R,D,C\subseteq V$. Define $s_a(x)=x-2B(x,a)B(a,a)^{-1}a$ and $W_R=\langle s\in\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf R}(V):\exists a\in R,\ \forall x,\ s(x)=s_a(x)\rangle$. A base $D$ of $R$ is a subset of $R$ which is real linearly independent, spans $V$, and such that for each $a\in R$ either $a$ or $-a$ is in the additive monoid generated by $D$ (equivalently, every root has an integral $D$-expansion of one sign). Put $R_D^+=R\cap\mathbf N D$ and $C_D=\{x:\forall a\in D,\ B(x,a)>0\}$. A chamber is a connected component of $\{x:\forall a\in R,\ B(x,a)\ne0\}$, with the usual real vector-space topology; explicitly $C$ is a chamber if it is the component of some point in this complement. These definitions include $R=\varnothing$. In the application $B$ is symmetric positive definite, $0\notin R$, and the displayed generators are the orthogonal root reflections.
